collections.intro_ar_source:
وهي مدنية، وعدد آياتها ٢٨٦.
لا خلاف بين أهل العلم في أن سورة البقرة مدنية، وهي من أوائل ما نزل بالمدينة، إلا قوله تعالى:
﴿وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ، ثُمَّ تُوَفَّى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا كَسَبَتْ، وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ [البقرة: ٢٨١].
فيقال: إنها آخر ما نزل من القرآن، وكذلك آيات الربا من آخر ما نزل.
مجموع ما جاء في فضائل سورة البقرة

collections.intro_en_source:
It is a Madinan sūrah consisting of 286 verses.
There is no disagreement among the scholars that Sūrat al-Baqarah is Madinan. It was among the earliest sūrahs revealed in Madinah, with the exception of the words of Allah, the Exalted:
“Be mindful of a Day when you will all be returned to Allah. Then every soul will be paid in full for what it has earned, and none will be wronged.”
 [Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:281]
It is said that this was the final verse of the Qur’an to be revealed. The verses concerning usury were likewise among the final revelations.
A Collection of Reports Concerning the Virtues of Sūrat al-Baqarah

collections.intro_ar_source:
وهي مدنية، وعدد آياتها ٧٥.
وقيل: إلا سبع آيات من قوله تعالى: ﴿وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ إلى سبع آيات، فإنها نزلت بمكة.
والأصح أنها نزلت بالمدينة، وإن كانت الواقعة بمكة، فإنها من إخبار الماضي.
الأنفال: جمع نفل، وهو في كلام العرب: كل إحسان فعله فاعل تفضلًا من غير أن يجب ذلك عليه.
وقد أحل اللّٰه الأنفال، وهي الغنائم، للمؤمنين من أموال عدوهم تكرمًا وتفضلًا على هذه الأمة، بعد أن كانت محرمة على الأمم السابقة.

collections.intro_en_source:
It is a Madinan sūrah consisting of 75 verses.
It has been said that seven verses, beginning with the words of Allah:
“And remember when those who disbelieved plotted against you,”
were revealed in Makkah.
The more correct view is that they were revealed in Madinah. Although the event itself occurred in Makkah, the verses relate an event from the past.
Al-Anfāl is the plural of nafl. In Arabic usage, it refers to every favor or act of kindness freely granted by someone without being obligatory upon him.
Allah made al-anfāl—the spoils of war taken from the enemy—lawful for the believers as an honor and favor granted to this nation, after such spoils had been forbidden to the previous nations.

collections.intro_ar_source:
وهي مدنية، وعدد آياتها ١٢٩.
وهي من أواخر ما نزل من القرآن، كما سيأتي في حديث البراء.
وقال ابن عباس: «التوبة هي الفاضحة».
ومما لا خلاف فيه أن البسملة لا تكتب قبل سورة التوبة.
وأما ما روي فيه قول ابن عباس لعثمان بن عفان رضي اللّٰه عنه: «ما حملكم أن عمدتم إلى الأنفال، وهي من المثاني، وإلى براءة، وهي من المئين، فقرنتم بينهما، ولم تكتبوا بينهما سطر بسم اللّٰه الرحمن الرحيم، ووضعتموها في السبع الطول، ما حملكم على ذلك؟».
فقال عثمان: «كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ مما يأتي عليه الزمان وهو ينزل عليه السور ذوات العدد، فكان إذا نزل عليه الشيء دعا بعض من كان يكتب، فيقول: ((ضعوا هؤلاء الآيات في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا)). وإذا نزلت عليه الآية، فيقول: ((ضعوا هذه الآية في السورة التي يذكر فيها كذا وكذا)).
وكانت الأنفال من أوائل ما أنزل بالمدينة، وكانت براءة من آخر القرآن، وكانت قصتها شبيهة بقصتها، فظننت أنها منها، فقُبض رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ولم يبين لنا أنها منها.
فمن أجل ذلك قرنت بينهما، ولم أكتب بينهما سطر بسم اللّٰه الرحمن الرحيم، فوضعتها في السبع الطول».
فهو ضعيف منكر.
رواه الترمذي (٣٠٨٦)، واللفظ له، وأبو داود (٧٨٦)، وأحمد (٣٩٩)، وابن حبان (٤٣)، والحاكم (٢/٢٢١).
وقال الترمذي: «هذا حديث حسن، لا نعرفه إلا من حديث عوف، عن يزيد الفارسي، عن ابن عباس. ويزيد الفارسي قد روى عن ابن عباس غير حديث، ويقال: هو يزيد بن هرمز، ويزيد الرقاشي هو يزيد بن أبان الرقاشي، ولم يدرك ابن عباس، ويزيد الفارسي أقدم من يزيد الرقاشي». انتهى.
قول الترمذي: يزيد الفارسي ليس هو يزيد الرقاشي، هذا صحيح لا خلاف فيه. وأما قوله: هو يزيد بن هرمز، فخالفه جمهور أهل العلم، فقالوا: يزيد الفارسي هذا لم يرو عنه سوى عوف بن أبي جميلة، فهو في عداد المجهولين، وهو غير يزيد بن هرمز الثقة من رواة مسلم، ومن قال: إنهما واحد فقد وهم.
وأما سكوت الحافظ ابن كثير بعد نقل الحديث في تفسيره، وتصحيح الحاكم له، فهو محل استغراب.
فإن في متنه أيضًا نكارة، فإن قول عثمان بأنه جعل سورة الأنفال والتوبة من الطوال مخالف لما ثبت بالتواتر أن ترتيب سور القرآن توقيفي؛ لأن النبي ﷺ عرض على جبريل في العرضة الأخيرة مرتين مرتبًا.

collections.intro_en_source:
It is a Madinan sūrah consisting of 129 verses.
It was among the last portions of the Qur’an to be revealed, as will be mentioned in the hadith of al-Barāʾ.
Ibn ʿAbbās said:
“Sūrat al-Tawbah is the exposer.”
There is no disagreement that the basmalah is not written at the beginning of Sūrat al-Tawbah.
As for the report in which Ibn ʿAbbās asked ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with him:
“What caused you to place al-Anfāl, which is among the mathānī, beside Barāʾah, which is among the sūrahs of approximately one hundred verses, joining them together without writing the line ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful’ between them, and placing them among the seven long sūrahs? What caused you to do that?”
ʿUthmān replied:
“Periods would pass during which sūrahs containing numerous verses were revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Whenever something was revealed to him, he would call one of his scribes and say:
‘Place these verses in the sūrah in which such-and-such is mentioned.’
When a verse was revealed, he would say:
‘Place this verse in the sūrah in which such-and-such is mentioned.’
“Al-Anfāl was among the earliest sūrahs revealed in Madinah, while Barāʾah was among the final portions of the Qur’an. Their subject matter was similar, so I thought that Barāʾah belonged with al-Anfāl. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away without clarifying to us whether it was part of it.
“For that reason, I joined the two together, did not write the line ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful’ between them, and placed them among the seven long sūrahs.”
This report is weak and objectionable.
Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3086), whose wording is cited, Abū Dāwūd (786), Aḥmad (399), Ibn Ḥibbān (43), and al-Ḥākim (2/221).
Al-Tirmidhī said:
“This is a good hadith. We know it only through the narration of ʿAwf, from Yazīd al-Fārisī, from Ibn ʿAbbās. Yazīd al-Fārisī narrated more than one hadith from Ibn ʿAbbās. It is said that he was Yazīd ibn Hurmuz. Yazīd al-Raqāshī was Yazīd ibn Abān al-Raqāshī, and he did not meet Ibn ʿAbbās. Yazīd al-Fārisī was earlier than Yazīd al-Raqāshī.”
End of al-Tirmidhī’s statement.
Al-Tirmidhī’s statement that Yazīd al-Fārisī was not Yazīd al-Raqāshī is correct and undisputed. However, his statement that he was Yazīd ibn Hurmuz was opposed by the majority of hadith scholars. They said that only ʿAwf ibn Abī Jamīlah narrated from this Yazīd al-Fārisī, so he is counted among the unknown narrators. He was not the trustworthy Yazīd ibn Hurmuz, one of Muslim’s narrators. Whoever claimed that they were the same person was mistaken.
As for al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Kathīr’s silence after quoting this hadith in his commentary, and al-Ḥākim’s authentication of it, both are surprising.
Its text also contains an objectionable element. ʿUthmān’s alleged statement that he placed Sūrat al-Anfāl and Sūrat al-Tawbah among the long sūrahs conflicts with what has been established through mass transmission: that the order of the Qur’anic sūrahs was determined through revelation. The Prophet ﷺ reviewed the Qur’an with Gabriel twice during the final review in its established order.

collections.intro_ar_source:
وهي مكية، وعدد آياتها ٩٨.
لما هاجر المسلمون إلى أرض الحبشة أرسل مشركو مكة في طلبهم رجلين جلدين، فكلما النجاشي ليردهم إلى بلادهم، ويسلمهم إلى أشراف قومهم. فاستفسر النجاشي المسلمين، فأجابه عنهم جعفر بن أبي طالب، وأخبره بما كان عليه حالهم قبل الإسلام، وما صاروا إليه بعد الإسلام، وما فعلته قريش تجاه المسلمين. فطلب النجاشي أن يقرأ عليه شيئًا مما جاء به نبيهم عن اللّٰه، فقرأ عليه سورة مريم.

لما هاجر المسلمون إلى أرض الحبشة أرسل مشركو مكة في طلبهم رجلين جلدين، فكلما النجاشي ليردهم إلى بلادهم، ويسلمهم إلى أشراف قومهم. فاستفسر النجاشي المسلمين، فأجابه عنهم جعفر بن أبي طالب، وأخبره بما كان عليه حالهم قبل الإسلام، وما صاروا إليه بعد الإسلام، وما فعلته قريش تجاه المسلمين. فطلب النجاشي أن يقرأ عليه شيئًا مما جاء به نبيهم عن اللّٰه، فقرأ عليه سورة مريم.
collections.intro_en_source:
It is a Makkan sūrah consisting of 98 verses.
When the Muslims emigrated to Abyssinia, the polytheists of Makkah sent two capable men after them. The two men spoke to the Negus and requested that he return the Muslims to their homeland and hand them over to the chiefs of their people.
The Negus questioned the Muslims, and Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib answered on their behalf. He informed him of their condition before Islam, what they had become after embracing Islam, and how Quraysh had treated the Muslims. The Negus then asked him to recite something that their Prophet had brought to them from Allah, so Jaʿfar recited Sūrat Maryam to him.

In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
“Did We not expand for you your chest, and remove from you your burden which weighed heavily upon your back, and raise high for you your mention? For indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease. So when you have finished, strive in worship, and direct your longing to your Lord alone.”
That is, We made your chest broad and spacious, illuminated with the light of guidance and knowledge.
This is like the words of Allah:
“Whoever Allah wills to guide, He opens his chest to Islam.” [Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:125]

It is a Madinan sūrah consisting of 8 verses.
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
“Those who disbelieved from among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to cease until the clear proof came to them: a Messenger from Allah reciting purified pages containing upright writings. Those who were given the Scripture did not divide until after the clear proof had come to them. Yet they were commanded only to worship Allah, devoting the religion sincerely to Him as people of pure monotheism, to establish prayer, and to give zakāh. That is the upright religion. Indeed, those who disbelieve among the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the Fire of Hell, remaining there forever. They are the worst of creation. Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds are the best of creation. Their reward with their Lord is Gardens of everlasting residence beneath which rivers flow, remaining there forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord.”

collections.intro_ar_source:
وهي مكية، وعدد آياتها ١١.
﴿بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾
﴿وَالْعَادِيَاتِ ضَبْحًا ۝ فَالْمُورِيَاتِ قَدْحًا ۝ فَالْمُغِيرَاتِ صُبْحًا ۝ فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعًا ۝ فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعًا ۝ إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ ۝ وَإِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ ۝ وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ ۝ أَفَلَا يَعْلَمُ إِذَا بُعْثِرَ مَا فِي الْقُبُورِ ۝ وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِي الصُّدُورِ ۝ إِنَّ رَبَّهُمْ بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَخَبِيرٌ﴾
قوله: ﴿وَالْعَادِيَاتِ ضَبْحًا﴾ جمع العادية، وهو اسم فاعل من العدو والسير السريع، ولذا قال جمع من القرين من الصحابة والتابعين وغيرهم: هي الخيل العادية في سبيل اللّٰه.
وقوله: ﴿ضَبْحًا﴾ من الضبح، وهو اضطراب النفس المتردد من الحنجرة دون أن يخرج من الفم، وهو من أصوات الخيل والسباع. قال ابن عباس: ليس شيء من الحيوانات تضبح غير الفرس والكلب والثعلب، وإنما تضبح هذه الحيوانات إذا تغير حالها من تعب أو فزع، وهو من قولهم: ضبحته النار إذا غيرت لونه.
قال علي بن أبي طالب وجماعة من التابعين وأتباعهم: هي الإبل. ويقال: إن ابن عباس رجع عن قوله الخيل إلى الإبل بعد أن ناقشه علي بن أبي طالب. والقول الأول رجحه ابن جرير وغيره.
وقوله: ﴿فَالْمُورِيَاتِ قَدْحًا﴾ القدح: حك الجسم على آخر ليقدح نارًا، يقال: قدح فأورى، والمراد الخيل التي توري النار بحوافرها إذا سارت في الحجارة.
وقوله: ﴿فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعًا﴾ أي: جمع الكفار من العدو.
وقوله: ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ﴾ هذا هو المقسم عليه، ومعناه: إنه لنعم ربه لجحود وكفور.
وقوله: ﴿لَكَنُودٌ﴾ من كند، وهو الكفور بالنعمة، يقال: أرض كنود، أي: الأرض التي لا تنبت شيئًا.
وقوله: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ﴾ الضمير عائد إلى الإنسان حسب الظاهر الذي يقتضيه اتساق الضمائر.
ولكن رأى جمهور أهل العلم أنه عائد إلى اللّٰه عز وجل، فإنه على ذلك لشهيد، أي: شاهد.
ويؤيد القول الأول قوله: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ﴾ أي: الإنسان، والخير هو المال، يعني: إن الإنسان شديد المحبة للمال.
وقوله: ﴿وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِي الصُّدُورِ﴾ أي: أبرز وأظهر ما في الصدور من خير أو شر.
وقوله: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّهُمْ بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَخَبِيرٌ﴾ قوله: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ أي: يوم الحساب ليحاسبهم ويجازيهم، واللّٰه خبير في ذلك اليوم وفي غيره.

collections.intro_en_source:
It is a Makkan sūrah consisting of 11 verses.
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
“By the charging horses, panting heavily, striking sparks with their hooves, raiding at dawn, stirring up clouds of dust, and penetrating into the midst of the enemy. Indeed, man is truly ungrateful to his Lord, and he himself is surely a witness to that. And indeed, he is intense in his love of wealth. Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered forth, and what is hidden within the hearts is brought out, their Lord will certainly be fully aware of them on that Day?”
Regarding the words:
“By the charging horses, panting heavily,”
al-ʿādiyāt is the plural of al-ʿādiyah, an active participle derived from running and moving swiftly.
For this reason, a group of the leading Companions, Tābiʿīn, and others said that it refers to horses charging swiftly in the cause of Allah.
Regarding:
“panting heavily,”
al-ḍabḥ is the rapid, agitated breathing that comes repeatedly from the throat without fully issuing from the mouth. It is among the sounds made by horses and predatory animals.
Ibn ʿAbbās said:
“No animals make this sound except the horse, the dog, and the fox.”
These animals make this sound when their condition changes because of exhaustion or fear.
The word is also related to the expression:
“The fire altered his color,”
when intense heat changes a person’s appearance.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and a group of the Tābiʿīn and their followers said that the verse refers to camels.

The first view—that it refers to horses—was preferred by Ibn Jarīr and others.

“striking sparks,”
al-qadḥ means rubbing or striking one object against another in order to produce fire.
It is said:

What is intended here are horses whose hooves produce sparks when striking stones as they run.

this means that they enter into the midst of the gathered enemy forces among the disbelievers.

this is the statement for which the preceding oaths were sworn.

comes from kanda, meaning to deny or show ingratitude for a blessing.

meaning land that produces nothing.

mean the Day of Reckoning, when Allah will call them to account and recompense them.

وهي مكية، وقيل: مدنية، وعدد آياتها ١١.
﴿بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾
﴿الْقَارِعَةُ ۝ مَا الْقَارِعَةُ ۝ وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْقَارِعَةُ ۝ يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ ۝ وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ ۝ فَأَمَّا مَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ ۝ فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ ۝ وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ ۝ فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ ۝ وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ ۝ نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ﴾
قوله: ﴿الْقَارِعَةُ﴾ من أسماء يوم القيامة كالحاقة والطامة والصاخة والغاشية وغيرها.
والقرع هو ضرب جسم بآخر بشدة لها صوت، وأطلق هنا على الحدث العظيم وهو يوم القيامة.
وقوله: ﴿يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ﴾ الفراش: فرخ الجراد حين يخرج من بيضه، وهو كما وصف اللّٰه تعالى: ﴿يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الْأَجْدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرَادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ﴾ [القمر: ٧].
وقوله: ﴿وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ﴾ أي: صارت كأنها الصوف المنفوش، الذي قد شرع في الذهاب والتمزق.
وقوله: ﴿فَأَمَّا مَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ﴾ أي: رجحت حسناته على سيئاته، وقد ورد ذكر الميزان للأعمال يوم القيامة كثيرًا في القرآن.
وقوله: ﴿فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ﴾ العيشة اسم مصدر العيش، كالخيفة اسم للخوف، والمراد بالعيشة الحياة.
وقوله: ﴿فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ﴾ أي: في حياة سعيدة طيبة في الجنة.
وقوله: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ﴾ أي: رجحت سيئاته على حسناته.
وقوله: ﴿فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ﴾ أي: ساقط هاو بأم رأسه في نار جهنم.
وهاوية هو: المكان المنخفض بين الجبلين الذي إذا سقط فيه إنسان أو دابة هلك. ويقال: سقط في الهاوية، يراد بها جهنم، وقيل: إنه اسم لجهنم.
وقوله: ﴿نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ﴾ حارة شديدة الحر، قوية اللهب، وقد وصف نار جهنم كما في الصحيح:

It is a Makkan sūrah, though it has also been said to be Madinan. It consists of 11 verses.
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
“The Striking Calamity! What is the Striking Calamity? And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is? On that Day people will be like scattered moths, and the mountains will be like fluffed wool. As for the one whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasant life. But as for the one whose scales are light, his abode will be the Abyss. And what will make you know what it is? A fiercely blazing Fire.”
Regarding:
“al-Qāriʿah,”
it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, like al-Ḥāqqah, al-Ṭāmmah, al-Ṣākhkhah, al-Ghāshiyah, and others.
Al-qarʿ means striking one object violently against another in a way that produces a sound.
Here the term is applied to the tremendous event of the Day of Resurrection.
Regarding:
“On that Day people will be like scattered moths,”
al-farāsh is also said to refer to young locusts when they first emerge from their eggs.
This is like the description given by Allah:
“They will come forth from the graves as though they were scattered locusts.” [Sūrat al-Qamar 54:7]
Regarding:
“And the mountains will be like fluffed wool,”
they will become like carded wool that has begun to scatter and come apart.
Regarding:
“As for the one whose scales are heavy,”
this means the one whose good deeds outweigh his bad deeds.
The weighing of deeds on the Day of Resurrection is mentioned frequently in the Qur’an.
Regarding:
“He will be in a pleasant life,”
al-ʿīshah is a verbal noun meaning life or living, just as al-khīfah is a noun meaning fear.
What is intended here is life itself.
Thus:
“He will be in a pleasant life”
means a happy and wholesome life in Paradise.
Regarding:
“But as for the one whose scales are light,”
this means the one whose bad deeds outweigh his good deeds.
Regarding:
“His abode will be the Abyss,”
this means that he will fall headfirst into the Fire of Hell.
A hāwiyah is a deep, low place between two mountains into which, if a person or animal falls, they perish.
The expression:
“He fell into al-Hāwiyah”
is used for falling into Hell.
It has also been said that al-Hāwiyah is itself one of the names of Hell.
Regarding:
“A fiercely blazing Fire,”
it means a fire of intense heat and powerful flame.
The Fire of Hell is described in the following authentic hadith:

وهي مكية عند جمهور أهل العلم، إلا أن البخاري يرى أنها مدنية، كما قال القرطبي في تفسيره، وعدد آياتها ٨.
﴿بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾
﴿أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ ۝ حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ ۝ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ ۝ ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ ۝ كَلَّا لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ ۝ لَتَرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ ۝ ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ ۝ ثُمَّ لَتُسْأَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ﴾
قوله: ﴿أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ﴾ عن طاعة ربكم وامتثال أوامره.
وقوله: ﴿حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ﴾ أي: صرتم من الميتين، ودفنتم في المقابر، والمقابر جمع مقبرة، والأرض التي فيها قبور كثيرة تسمى مقبرة.
وقوله: ﴿كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ ليس الأمر كما ظننتم بأن الأمر بالتكاثر والتفاخر، بل ستعلمون قريبًا بطلان ما كنتم ظننتم. وقوله: ﴿ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ التكرار للتأكيد.
وقوله: ﴿كَلَّا لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ﴾ جواب لو محذوف، أي: لو تعلمون علمًا يقينًا لشغلكم ما تعلمون عن التكاثر والتفاخر. وإضافة ﴿عِلْمَ﴾ إلى ﴿الْيَقِينِ﴾ إضافة بيانية، فإن اليقين علم، أي: لو علمتم علمًا مطابقًا للواقع لما صارت هذه حالكم.
المخاطبون في هذه الآيات كفار مكة الذين كفروا باللّٰه، ولم يؤمنوا بهذا النبي الكريم الذي جاء ليخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور. وفيه تحذير شديد للمؤمنين الذين يشغلهم التكاثر في الأموال والأولاد، وأنهم سوف يسألون يوم القيامة عن النعم إلا من رحمه اللّٰه، وأدى حق أنعمه.

وقوله: ﴿كَلَّا لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ﴾ جواب لو محذوف، أي: لو تعلمون علمًا يقينًا لشغلكم ما تعلمون عن التكاثر والتفاخر. وإضافة ﴿عِلْمَ﴾ إلى ﴿الْيَقِينِ﴾ إضافة بيانية، فإن اليقين علم، أي: لو علمتم علمًا مطابقًا للواقع لما صارت هذه حالكم.
المخاطبون في هذه الآيات كفار مكة الذين كفروا باللّٰه، ولم يؤمنوا بهذا النبي الكريم الذي جاء ليخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور. وفيه تحذير شديد للمؤمنين الذين يشغلهم التكاثر في الأموال والأولاد، وأنهم سوف يسألون يوم القيامة عن النعم إلا من رحمه اللّٰه، وأدى حق أنعمه.
collections.intro_en_source:
It is a Makkan sūrah according to the majority of scholars, although al-Bukhārī regarded it as Madinan, as al-Qurṭubī stated in his commentary. It consists of 8 verses.
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
“Competition for more has distracted you, until you visit the graves. No! You will soon know. Again, no! You will soon know. No! If only you knew with certain knowledge. You will surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty. Then, on that Day, you will surely be questioned about the blessings you enjoyed.”
Regarding the words:
“Competition for more has distracted you,”
it has distracted you from obeying your Lord and carrying out His commands.
Regarding:
“Until you visit the graves,”
this means until you become among the dead and are buried in the graveyards.
Al-maqābir is the plural of maqbarah, and land containing many graves is called a graveyard.
Regarding:
“No! You will soon know,”
the matter is not as you imagined—that life is about competing and boasting in abundance. You will soon come to know the falsehood of what you imagined.
The repetition in:
“Again, no! You will soon know”
is for emphasis.
Regarding:
“No! If only you knew with certain knowledge,”
the response to “if” is omitted.
The meaning is: if you truly possessed certain knowledge, what you knew would have occupied you away from competing and boasting.
The construction “knowledge of certainty” is explanatory, for certainty itself is knowledge. In other words, if you possessed knowledge fully corresponding to reality, you would not have ended up in this condition.
Those directly addressed in these verses are the disbelievers of Makkah who disbelieved in Allah and did not believe in this noble Prophet who came to bring them out of darkness into light.
The verses also contain a severe warning to believers who become distracted by competing in wealth and children. They will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about the blessings they were given, except those upon whom Allah has mercy and who fulfill the rights of His blessings.

collections.intro_ar_source:
وهي مكية، وعدد آياتها ٣.
﴿بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾
﴿وَالْعَصْرِ ۝ إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ ۝ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾
سورة العصر هي إحدى سور ثلاث هن أقصر السور، وعدد آياتها ثلاث، هي والكوثر والنصر.
وسورة العصر مع قصرها تشتمل على أهم ثلاثة أمور في حياة الإنسان، وهي:
١- الخسران للكفار والمشركين.
٢- النجاة للمؤمنين.
٣- الصبر على ما يصيب الإنسان في التواصي بالخير.
ولذا كان الإمام الشافعي يقول: لو لم ينزل إلى الناس إلا هي لكفتهم، وفي رواية: لو تدبر الناس هذه السورة لوسعتهم. وقال غيره: إنها شملت جميع علوم القرآن.
قوله: ﴿وَالْعَصْرِ﴾ أي: أقسم اللّٰه تعالى بالعصر، والمراد منه الدهر، كما قال ابن عباس، وهو الظاهر.
وإن كان العصر استعمل لمعان عدة، وأشهرها آخر النهار، وهو وقت صلاة العصر.
وقوله: ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ﴾ أي: جنس الإنسان، وهو يستغرق جميع أفراد الإنسان عند نزول هذه الآية الكريمة ومن جاء بعدهم، سواء بلغتهم الدعوة ومن لم تبلغهم، فالخسران صفة لازمة للإنسان، والخسر هو الهلكة، وقيل: العقوبة، ومنه قوله تعالى: ﴿وَكَانَ عَاقِبَةُ أَمْرِهَا خُسْرًا﴾ [الطلاق: ٩].
وقوله: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾ استثنى من الخسران الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات، وبقي حكم الخسران متحققًا في غير المؤمنين على مر الدهور إلى يوم القيامة. وهذه مناسبة للقسم بالعصر، أي: الدهر.
وقوله: ﴿وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ﴾ التواصي بالحق من الأعمال الصالحة، وقد يلحقه الأذى والمشقة كما حصلت للأنبياء عليهم السلام، ومن على طريقتهم في الدعوة والتبليغ، فأمروا بالتواصي بالصبر؛ لأن الصبر مفتاح النجاح، ولذا أمر اللّٰه تعالى في سورة البقرة [٤٥]: ﴿وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ﴾.
روي عن أبي مدينة الدارمي - وكانت له صحبة - قال: كان الرجلان من أصحاب النبي ﷺ إذا التقيا لم يفترقا حتى يقرأ أحدهما على الآخر: ﴿وَالْعَصْرِ ۝ إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ﴾، ثم يسلم أحدهما على الآخر.

collections.intro_en_source:
It is a Makkan sūrah consisting of 3 verses.
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
“By time. Indeed, mankind is surely in loss, except those who believe, do righteous deeds, urge one another to the truth, and urge one another to patience.”
Sūrat al-ʿAṣr is one of three sūrahs that are among the shortest in the Qur’an. Each consists of three verses: al-ʿAṣr, al-Kawthar, and al-Naṣr.
Despite its brevity, Sūrat al-ʿAṣr contains three of the most important matters in human life:
Loss for the disbelievers and polytheists.
Salvation for the believers.
Patience regarding what afflicts a person while urging others toward goodness.
For this reason, Imām al-Shāfiʿī used to say:
“Had nothing been revealed to mankind except this sūrah, it would have been sufficient for them.”
In another wording:
“If people truly reflected upon this sūrah, it would suffice them.”
Others said:
“It encompasses all the sciences and teachings of the Qur’an.”
Regarding:
“By al-ʿAṣr,”
Allah, the Exalted, swears by al-ʿaṣr.
What is meant is time itself, as Ibn ʿAbbās said, and this is the apparent meaning.
The word al-ʿaṣr is used for several meanings, the most famous of which is the latter part of the day, which is the time of the ʿAṣr prayer.
Regarding:
“Indeed, mankind is surely in loss,”
the word man refers to humankind as a whole.
It encompasses every human being alive when this noble verse was revealed and everyone who came after them, whether the message reached them or did not reach them.
Loss is therefore the general condition of mankind.
Al-khusr means destruction and ruin, and it has also been said to mean punishment.
From this is the statement of Allah:
“And the outcome of its affair was loss.” [Sūrat al-Ṭalāq 65:9]
Regarding:
“Except those who believe and do righteous deeds,”
those who believe and perform righteous deeds are excluded from the general loss.
The judgment of loss remains applicable to those outside faith throughout the ages until the Day of Resurrection.
This corresponds to the oath by al-ʿaṣr, meaning time or the ages.
Regarding:
“And urge one another to the truth and urge one another to patience,”
mutually encouraging one another toward truth is itself among righteous deeds.
It may bring harm and hardship, as happened to the Prophets عليهم السلام and to those who follow their path in calling and conveying the message.
Therefore, they are commanded to encourage one another to patience, because patience is a key to success.
For this reason Allah says in Sūrat al-Baqarah [2:45]:
“Seek help through patience and prayer.”
It is narrated from Abū Madīnah al-Dārimī, who was a Companion, that he said:
“When two men from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ met, they would not part from one another until one of them recited to the other: ‘By time. Indeed, mankind is surely in loss…’ Then one would give salām to the other.”

collections.intro_ar_source:
وهي مكية، وعدد آياتها ٩.
﴿بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾
﴿وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ ۝ الَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ ۝ يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ ۝ كَلَّا لَيُنْبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ ۝ وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحُطَمَةُ ۝ نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ ۝ الَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ ۝ إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ ۝ فِي عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ﴾
قوله: ﴿وَيْلٌ﴾ هو الخزي والعذاب والهلكة والدعاء على المجرور.
وقوله: ﴿لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ﴾ قال ابن عباس: هم المشاؤون بالنميمة، المفسدون بين الأحبة.
والهمزة: على وزن فُعلة، وهي صيغة تدل على كثرة صدور هذا الفعل، وهو مشتق من الهمز.
وقوله: ﴿لُمَزَةٍ﴾ من اللمز، يقال: إن الهمزة الذي يغتاب بالغيبة، واللمزة: الذي يغتاب في الوجه.
وقال سفيان الثوري: الهمزة الذي يهمز بلسانه، واللمزة الذي يلمز بعينيه.
والوصف الجامع للهمزة اللمزة كثرة الغيبة، وقد اشتهر الكفار والمشركون بهذين الوصفين لأذى المسلمين، وهما من الصفات الذميمة، يجب على المسلم أن يجتنب منهما.
وقوله: ﴿الَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ هي لزيادة تشنيع للهمازين واللمازين، الذين جمعوا المال، ولم يؤدوا حقه، مثل قوله تعالى: ﴿وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰ﴾ [المعارج: ١٨].
وقوله: ﴿وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ أي: أحصاه، وأكثر من عده لشدة ولعه بجمعه، فالتضعيف للمبالغة في عد.
وقوله: ﴿يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ﴾ أي: أنه يظن أن ماله يبقيه حيًا لا يموت؛ لأن الخلود في الدنيا أقصى ما يتمناه الكافر بخلاف المؤمن.
وقوله: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ فيه إبطال ما ظنوه.
وقوله: ﴿لَيُنْبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ﴾ النبذ هو الإلقاء والطرح، وهو أكثر ما يستعمل في المكروه، كقوله تعالى: ﴿فَأَخَذْنَاهُ وَجُنُودَهُ فَنَبَذْنَاهُمْ فِي الْيَمِّ﴾ [القصص: ٤٠].
والحطمة: على وزن فُعلة مثل الهمزة. والحطمة هي نار اللّٰه، سميت بذلك لأنها تكسر كل ما يلقى فيها فتحطمه، وهي من أسماء جهنم، ودرجتها غير معلومة، وما قيل فيها كله ظن وخرص.
وقوله: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحُطَمَةُ﴾ للتعظيم لشأنها، والتفخيم لأمرها، والاستفهام يفيد تهويل الحطمة.
وقوله: ﴿نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ﴾ جواب عن جملة: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحُطَمَةُ﴾.
وقوله: ﴿الْمُوقَدَةُ﴾ اسم مفعول من أوقد النار، إذا أشعلها وألهبها.

It is a Makkan sūrah consisting of 9 verses.
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
“Woe to every slanderer and mocker, who gathers wealth and repeatedly counts it, thinking that his wealth will make him immortal. No! He will surely be thrown into al-Ḥuṭamah. And what will make you know what al-Ḥuṭamah is? It is the kindled Fire of Allah, which rises over the hearts. Indeed, it will be closed in upon them, in extended columns.”
Regarding:
“Woe,”
it means disgrace, punishment, destruction, and an invocation of ruin against the one being condemned.
Regarding:
“To every humazah and lumazah,”
Ibn ʿAbbās said:
“They are those who go about spreading malicious gossip and causing corruption between people who love one another.”
Humazah follows the Arabic morphological pattern fuʿalah, which indicates frequent repetition of the action. It is derived from hamz.
Regarding:
“lumazah,”
it is derived from lamz.
It has been said that the humazah is the one who speaks ill of people behind their backs, whereas the lumazah is the one who insults and disparages them to their faces.
Sufyān al-Thawrī said:
“The humazah is the one who attacks others with his tongue, while the lumazah is the one who mocks or disparages others with his eyes.”
The general characteristic shared by the humazah and lumazah is frequent backbiting and disparagement.
The disbelievers and polytheists became known for these two behaviors in their abuse of the Muslims.
They are reprehensible traits that a Muslim must avoid.
Regarding:
“Who gathers wealth and repeatedly counts it,”
this further condemns those slanderers and mockers who accumulate wealth without fulfilling its rights.
It is similar to the words of Allah:
“And gathered wealth and hoarded it.” [Sūrat al-Maʿārij 70:18]
Regarding:
“And repeatedly counts it,”
this means that he carefully calculates it and continually recounts it because of his intense attachment to accumulating it.
The doubled form of the verb conveys repeated and excessive counting.
Regarding:
“Thinking that his wealth will make him immortal,”
he imagines that his wealth will keep him alive and prevent him from dying.
Remaining forever in this world is among the greatest wishes of the disbeliever, unlike the believer.
Regarding:
“No!”
it completely rejects and nullifies what they imagined.
Regarding:
“He will surely be thrown into al-Ḥuṭamah,”
al-nabdh means casting or throwing something away and is most commonly used in undesirable contexts.
It is like the words of Allah:
“So We seized him and his soldiers and cast them into the sea.” [Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ 28:40]
Al-Ḥuṭamah follows the same morphological pattern fuʿalah as al-humazah.
Al-Ḥuṭamah is the Fire of Allah. It is called this because it crushes and destroys everything thrown into it.
It is one of the names of Hell.
Its particular level or rank within Hell is not known, and everything claimed concerning that without evidence is merely conjecture and speculation.
Regarding:
“And what will make you know what al-Ḥuṭamah is?”
this magnifies its significance and emphasizes the enormity of its affair.
The question conveys the terrifying nature of al-Ḥuṭamah.
The words:
“The kindled Fire of Allah”
are the answer to:
“And what will make you know what al-Ḥuṭamah is?”
Regarding:
“kindled,”
it is the passive participle of the verb meaning to ignite and inflame a fire.
Describing the Fire as “kindled” indicates that it remains continually burning and never goes out.
Regarding:
“Which rises over the hearts,”
it means that the Fire will burn through them until it reaches their hearts while they remain alive.
Regarding:
“Indeed, it will be closed in upon them,”
this may be understood as a third description of the Fire of Allah.
Muʾṣadah is the passive participle of the verb meaning to close a door firmly and completely.
Regarding:
“In extended columns,”
the preposition is understood here with the meaning of “by” or “with”; that is, the Fire is sealed over them with extended columns.
Ibn Masʿūd said this, and his recitation was:
“With extended columns.”
Ibn ʿAbbās said that the extended columns are shackles placed around their necks.
All of these descriptions convey the extreme severity of the punishment imposed upon them.

وهي مكية، وعدد آياتها ٥.
﴿بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾
﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَابِ الْفِيلِ ۝ أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ كَيْدَهُمْ فِي تَضْلِيلٍ ۝ وَأَرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ ۝ تَرْمِيهِمْ بِحِجَارَةٍ مِنْ سِجِّيلٍ ۝ فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَأْكُولٍ﴾
إن اللّٰه تعالى امتن على قريش خاصة، وأهل مكة عامة، بأنه صرف عنهم أصحاب الفيل، وهو أبرهة وأصحابه، الذين كانوا قد عزموا على هدم الكعبة، ومحو أثرها من الوجود، وقصدوا مكة ومعهم فيل عظيم كبير الجثة لم ير مثله، وكان قد بعثه إليه النجاشي ملك الحبشة، وكان معه أيضًا عدد من الأفيال.
فلما انتهى أبرهة إلى المغمس - وهو قريب من مكة - نزل به، وأغار جيشه على سرح أهل مكة من الإبل وغيرها، فأخذوه، وكان في السرح مائتا بعير لعبد المطلب، وكان الذي أغار على السرح بأمر أبرهة أمير المقدمة، وكان يقال له: الأسود بن مقصود، فهجاه بعض العرب - فيما ذكره ابن إسحاق -.
وبعث أبرهة حناطة الحميري إلى مكة، وأمره أن يأتيه بأشرف قريش، وأن يخبره أن الملك لم يجئ لقتالكم إلا أن تصدوه عن البيت.
فجاء حناطة، فدل على عبد المطلب بن هاشم، وبلغه عن أبرهة ما قال، فقال له عبد المطلب: واللّٰه ما نريد حربه، وما لنا بذلك من طاقة، هذا بيت اللّٰه الحرام، وبيت خليله إبراهيم، فإن يمنعه منه فهو بيته وحرمه، وإن يخل بينه وبينه، فواللّٰه ما عندنا دفع عنه.
فقال له حناطة: فاذهب معي إليه، فذهب معه، فلما رآه أبرهة أجله، وكان عبد المطلب رجلًا جسيمًا حسن المنظر.
ونزل أبرهة عن سريره، وجلس معه على البساط، وقال لترجمانه: قل له: ما حاجتك؟
فقال للترجمان: إن حاجتي أن يرد علي الملك مائتي بعير أصابها لي.
فقال أبرهة لترجمانه: قل له: لقد كنت أعجبتني حين رأيتك، ثم قد زهدت فيك حين كلمتني، أتكلمني في مائتي بعير أصبتها لك، وتترك بيتًا هو دينك ودين آبائك قد جئت لهدمه، لا تكلمني فيه؟!
فقال له عبد المطلب: إني أنا رب الإبل، وإن للبيت ربًا سيمنعه.
قال: ما كان ليمتنع مني!
قال: أنت وذاك.
فلما أراد أبرهة وجيشه دخول مكة أرسل اللّٰه عليهم طيرًا من البحر مثل الخطاطيف والبلسان، مع كل طائر منها ثلاثة أحجار يحملها: حجر في منقاره، وحجران في رجليه، أمثال الحمص والعدس، لا تصيب منهم أحدًا إلا هلك.
فهلك معظم الجيش، وأدبر الباقون، وكان ممن أصاب أبرهة نفسه، فخرجوا به حتى قدموا صنعاء، وهو مثل فرخ الطائر، فما مات حتى صدع صدره عن قلبه.
وغنم قريش مالًا كثيرًا من أسلابهم.
هكذا كفى اللّٰه أهل مكة أمر عدوهم، وكان ذلك في شهر المحرم الموافق شهر فبراير سنة ٥٧٠م.
وبعد هذه الحادثة العظيمة بخمسين يومًا ولد سيد البشر محمد بن عبد اللّٰه صلوات اللّٰه وسلامه عليه في أصح أقوال أهل العلم.
قوله: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَابِ الْفِيلِ﴾ الخطاب للنبي ﷺ، وقد تواترت الأخبار عن قصة أصحاب الفيل عند أهل مكة، وبقيت بعض آثارها شاهدة عليها، والنبي ﷺ خاطب قريشًا بهذه القصة.
وقوله: ﴿أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ كَيْدَهُمْ فِي تَضْلِيلٍ﴾ أي: إن ربك هو الذي أبطل ما أرادوا مع قوتهم وبأسهم.
وفيه تطمين للنبي ﷺ بأن اللّٰه قادر على كل شيء، وقد جاء في الصحيح:

فلما انتهى أبرهة إلى المغمس - وهو قريب من مكة - نزل به، وأغار جيشه على سرح أهل مكة من الإبل وغيرها، فأخذوه، وكان في السرح مائتا بعير لعبد المطلب، وكان الذي أغار على السرح بأمر أبرهة أمير المقدمة، وكان يقال له: الأسود بن مقصود، فهجاه بعض العرب - فيما ذكره ابن إسحاق -.
وبعث أبرهة حناطة الحميري إلى مكة، وأمره أن يأتيه بأشرف قريش، وأن يخبره أن الملك لم يجئ لقتالكم إلا أن تصدوه عن البيت.
فجاء حناطة، فدل على عبد المطلب بن هاشم، وبلغه عن أبرهة ما قال، فقال له عبد المطلب: واللّٰه ما نريد حربه، وما لنا بذلك من طاقة، هذا بيت اللّٰه الحرام، وبيت خليله إبراهيم، فإن يمنعه منه فهو بيته وحرمه، وإن يخل بينه وبينه، فواللّٰه ما عندنا دفع عنه.
فقال له حناطة: فاذهب معي إليه، فذهب معه، فلما رآه أبرهة أجله، وكان عبد المطلب رجلًا جسيمًا حسن المنظر.
ونزل أبرهة عن سريره، وجلس معه على البساط، وقال لترجمانه: قل له: ما حاجتك؟
فقال للترجمان: إن حاجتي أن يرد علي الملك مائتي بعير أصابها لي.
فقال أبرهة لترجمانه: قل له: لقد كنت أعجبتني حين رأيتك، ثم قد زهدت فيك حين كلمتني، أتكلمني في مائتي بعير أصبتها لك، وتترك بيتًا هو دينك ودين آبائك قد جئت لهدمه، لا تكلمني فيه؟!
فقال له عبد المطلب: إني أنا رب الإبل، وإن للبيت ربًا سيمنعه.
قال: ما كان ليمتنع مني!
قال: أنت وذاك.
فلما أراد أبرهة وجيشه دخول مكة أرسل اللّٰه عليهم طيرًا من البحر مثل الخطاطيف والبلسان، مع كل طائر منها ثلاثة أحجار يحملها: حجر في منقاره، وحجران في رجليه، أمثال الحمص والعدس، لا تصيب منهم أحدًا إلا هلك.
فهلك معظم الجيش، وأدبر الباقون، وكان ممن أصاب أبرهة نفسه، فخرجوا به حتى قدموا صنعاء، وهو مثل فرخ الطائر، فما مات حتى صدع صدره عن قلبه.
وغنم قريش مالًا كثيرًا من أسلابهم.
هكذا كفى اللّٰه أهل مكة أمر عدوهم، وكان ذلك في شهر المحرم الموافق شهر فبراير سنة ٥٧٠م.
وبعد هذه الحادثة العظيمة بخمسين يومًا ولد سيد البشر محمد بن عبد اللّٰه صلوات اللّٰه وسلامه عليه في أصح أقوال أهل العلم.
قوله: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَابِ الْفِيلِ﴾ الخطاب للنبي ﷺ، وقد تواترت الأخبار عن قصة أصحاب الفيل عند أهل مكة، وبقيت بعض آثارها شاهدة عليها، والنبي ﷺ خاطب قريشًا بهذه القصة.
وقوله: ﴿أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ كَيْدَهُمْ فِي تَضْلِيلٍ﴾ أي: إن ربك هو الذي أبطل ما أرادوا مع قوتهم وبأسهم.
وفيه تطمين للنبي ﷺ بأن اللّٰه قادر على كل شيء، وقد جاء في الصحيح:

It is a Makkan sūrah consisting of 5 verses.
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
“Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the people of the elephant? Did He not make their scheme go utterly astray? He sent against them flocks of birds, pelting them with stones of baked clay, and made them like chewed-up straw.”
Allah, the Exalted, bestowed a particular favor upon Quraysh, and upon the people of Makkah generally, by turning away from them the People of the Elephant—Abrahah and his forces—who had resolved to demolish the Kaʿbah and erase its trace from existence.
They marched toward Makkah with a massive elephant of extraordinary size, the like of which had not been seen. The Negus, king of Abyssinia, had sent it to Abrahah, and a number of other elephants were with it as well.
When Abrahah reached al-Mughammis, a place near Makkah, he encamped there.
His army raided the grazing livestock of the people of Makkah, including their camels, and seized them. Among those animals were two hundred camels belonging to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
The commander who carried out the raid upon Abrahah’s orders was the leader of the vanguard, a man called al-Aswad ibn Maqṣūd. Some of the Arabs later satirized him in poetry, as Ibn Isḥāq mentioned.
Abrahah sent Ḥunāṭah al-Ḥimyarī to Makkah and instructed him to bring back the most honored man of Quraysh and to inform him:
“The king has not come to fight you unless you prevent him from reaching the House.”
Ḥunāṭah came and was directed to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim. He conveyed to him what Abrahah had said.
ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib replied:
“By Allah, we do not intend to fight him, nor do we have the strength to do so. This is the Sacred House of Allah and the House of His intimate friend Ibrāhīm. If Allah protects it from him, then it is His House and His sanctuary. But if He allows him access to it, then by Allah, we have no power to defend it.”
Ḥunāṭah said:
“Then come with me to him.”
So ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib went with him.
When Abrahah saw him, he held him in great respect, for ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib was a large and impressive man of handsome appearance.
Abrahah came down from his throne and sat with him upon the carpet.
He said to his interpreter:
“Ask him what he needs.”
ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said to the interpreter:
“My request is that the king return to me the two hundred camels of mine that he seized.”
Abrahah said to his interpreter:
“Tell him: When I first saw you, I was impressed by you. But after hearing you speak, I have lost respect for you. You speak to me about two hundred camels of yours that I have taken, yet you say nothing about a House that is the religion of you and your forefathers, which I have come to demolish?”
ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib replied:
“I am the owner of the camels, and the House has a Lord who will protect it.”
Abrahah said:
“It cannot be protected from me!”
ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib replied:
“That is between you and Him.”
When Abrahah and his army intended to enter Makkah, Allah sent against them birds from the direction of the sea, resembling swallows and balsān birds.
Each bird carried three stones: one in its beak and two in its feet. They were about the size of chickpeas and lentils.
No one among the army was struck by one of those stones except that he perished.
Most of the army was destroyed, while the survivors fled.
Abrahah himself was among those afflicted. They carried him away until they reached Ṣanʿāʾ, while his body had deteriorated until he was like a young bird.
He did not die until his chest split open and exposed his heart.
Quraysh obtained a great deal of wealth from the spoils they left behind.
Thus Allah sufficed the people of Makkah against their enemy.
The author states that this occurred in the month of Muḥarram, corresponding to February of the year 570 CE.
According to what the author regards as the strongest view among the scholars, fifty days after this tremendous event, the master of mankind, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh ﷺ, was born.
Regarding the words:
“Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the people of the elephant?”
the address is directed to the Prophet ﷺ.
Reports concerning the story of the People of the Elephant were widespread and recurrent among the people of Makkah, and some traces of the event remained as evidence of it.
The Prophet ﷺ addressed Quraysh with this story.
Regarding:
“Did He not make their scheme go utterly astray?”
this means that your Lord is the One who nullified what they intended despite their strength and military might.
This also contains reassurance for the Prophet ﷺ that Allah has power over all things.
It is stated in the authentic hadith:

وهي مكية، وعدد آياتها ٧.
﴿بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾
﴿أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ ۝ فَذَٰلِكَ الَّذِي يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ ۝ وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ ۝ فَوَيْلٌ لِلْمُصَلِّينَ ۝ الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ ۝ الَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَاءُونَ ۝ وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ﴾
قوله: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ﴾ فيه استنكار من اللّٰه تعالى على الذين يكذبون بالدين، وهو المعاد والجزاء والثواب، ثم بيّن بعض صفات هؤلاء، فقال: ﴿فَذَٰلِكَ الَّذِي يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ﴾ أي: يدفع اليتيم ولا يحسن إليه.
ومعنى ﴿يَدُعُّ﴾ يدفع بعنف وقهر، كقوله تعالى: ﴿يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا﴾ [الطور: ١٣]، من الأخلاق السيئة لهؤلاء المكذبين بيوم الدين.
وقوله: ﴿وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ﴾ الحض: الحث، ونفي الحض يستلزم نفي الإطعام، وهو من الأخلاق السيئة لهؤلاء المكذبين بيوم الدين.
وقوله: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلْمُصَلِّينَ ۝ الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنْ صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ﴾:
١- المراد منه المنافقون الذين يؤخرون الصلاة عن وقتها.
٢- أو لا يؤدون الصلاة بأركانها وشروطها خاشعين وخاضعين.
٣- أو يتركون الصلاة أصلًا إذا كان في السر لا يراه غيرهم.
والأحاديث الواردة في صلاة المنافقين كثيرة جدًا، منها ما جاء في الصحيح:

It is a Makkan sūrah consisting of 7 verses.
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
“Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? That is the one who harshly repulses the orphan and does not encourage the feeding of the poor. So woe to those who pray, yet are heedless of their prayer—those who only show off and withhold even small acts of assistance.”
Regarding:
“Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?”
this contains Allah’s condemnation of those who deny al-dīn, meaning resurrection, recompense, and reward.
Allah then explains some of their characteristics, saying:
“That is the one who harshly repulses the orphan,”
meaning that he pushes the orphan away and does not treat him kindly.
The word:
“yaduʿʿu”
means to push or drive someone violently and harshly, as Allah says:
“On the Day they will be violently thrust into the Fire of Hell.” [Sūrat al-Ṭūr 52:13]
This is among the evil characteristics of those who deny the Day of Recompense.
Regarding:
“And does not encourage the feeding of the poor,”
al-ḥaḍḍ means urging and encouraging.
The fact that he does not even encourage others to feed the poor necessarily indicates that he himself does not feed them.
This too is among the evil characteristics of those who deny the Day of Recompense.
Regarding the words:
“So woe to those who pray, those who are heedless of their prayer”:
What is meant may be the hypocrites who delay the prayer beyond its proper time.
Or those who do not perform the prayer properly with its essential pillars and conditions, with humility and submission.
Or those who abandon the prayer entirely when they are in private and no one can see them.
There are very many hadiths concerning the prayer of the hypocrites. Among them is the following authentic report:

It is a Makkan sūrah consisting of 7 verses.
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
“Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? That is the one who harshly repulses the orphan and does not encourage the feeding of the poor. So woe to those who pray, yet are heedless of their prayer—those who only show off and withhold even small acts of assistance.”
Regarding:
“Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?”
this contains Allah’s condemnation of those who deny al-dīn, meaning resurrection, recompense, and reward.
Allah then explains some of their characteristics, saying:
“That is the one who harshly repulses the orphan,”
meaning that he pushes the orphan away and does not treat him kindly.
The word:
“yaduʿʿu”
means to push or drive someone violently and harshly, as Allah says:
“On the Day they will be violently thrust into the Fire of Hell.” [Sūrat al-Ṭūr 52:13]
This is among the evil characteristics of those who deny the Day of Recompense.
Regarding:
“And does not encourage the feeding of the poor,”
al-ḥaḍḍ means urging and encouraging.
The fact that he does not even encourage others to feed the poor necessarily indicates that he himself does not feed them.
This too is among the evil characteristics of those who deny the Day of Recompense.
Regarding the words:
“So woe to those who pray, those who are heedless of their prayer”:
What is meant may be the hypocrites who delay the prayer beyond its proper time.
Or those who do not perform the prayer properly with its essential pillars and conditions, with humility and submission.
Or those who abandon the prayer entirely when they are in private and no one can see them.

“When the help of Allah comes and the conquest, and you see the people entering the religion of Allah in crowds, then glorify your Lord with praise and seek His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever accepting of repentance.”

“If he prevails over his own people, then he is truly a Prophet.”
When Allah granted him the conquest of Makkah, they entered the religion of Allah in crowds.

It is a Makkan sūrah consisting of 5 verses.
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
“May the hands of Abū Lahab perish, and perish he did. Neither his wealth nor what he earned will benefit him. He will burn in a flaming Fire, and so will his wife, the carrier of firewood, around her neck a rope of tightly twisted fiber.”
Abū Lahab was ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, one of the paternal uncles of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He was intensely hostile toward the Prophet ﷺ and caused him great harm. Allah, the Exalted, therefore condemned him with this tremendous condemnation, which remains a disgrace upon him until the Day of Resurrection.
His kunyah was Abū ʿUtbah, after his son. As for the kunyah Abū Lahab, Allah willed that his ultimate destination would be the Fire, and he had already become known by this kunyah during the Jāhiliyyah, as stated in the hadith of Rabīʿah ibn ʿAbbād.
The Qur’an addressed him by this name.

It is a Madinan sūrah consisting of 6 verses.
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
“Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws, who whispers into the hearts of mankind, from among jinn and mankind.”
This sūrah mentions three of the attributes of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
Lordship, Kingship, and Divinity.
He is the Lord of everything, its King, and the One uniquely deserving of worship.
Thus, the one seeking refuge is commanded to seek refuge in the One possessing these attributes from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws, namely the devil assigned to the human being.
Al-khannās means one who repeatedly withdraws and hides.
Al-khuns and al-khunūs mean concealment or disappearance.
It is a description of Satan because he whispers into souls and minds without appearing openly.
There is no human being from the children of Ādam except that he has a companion who beautifies indecencies for him, while the one protected is the one whom Allah protects.
This is stated in the authentic hadith:

It is a Madinan sūrah consisting of 6 verses.
In the Name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
“Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws, who whispers into the hearts of mankind, from among jinn and mankind.”
This sūrah mentions three of the attributes of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
Lordship, Kingship, and Divinity.
He is the Lord of everything, its King, and the One uniquely deserving of worship.
Thus, the one seeking refuge is commanded to seek refuge in the One possessing these attributes from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws, namely the devil assigned to the human being.
Al-khannās means one who repeatedly withdraws and hides.
Al-khuns and al-khunūs mean concealment or disappearance.
It is a description of Satan because he whispers into souls and minds without appearing openly.
There is no human being from the children of Ādam except that he has a companion who beautifies indecencies for him, while the one protected is the one whom Allah protects.
This is stated in the authentic hadith:

لها ثلاثة أسماء معروفة، وهي: فاتحة الكتاب، وأم القرآن، والسبع المثاني. وتسمى أيضًا أم الكتاب.
قال البخاري رحمه اللّٰه تعالى في تفسير سورة الفاتحة: «وسميت أم الكتاب؛ لأنه يبدأ بكتابتها في المصاحف، ويبدأ بقراءتها في الصلاة».
وتسمى أيضًا، كما جاء في الآثار: الكنز، والوافية، والشافية، والكافية، والحمد، والحمد للّٰه، والصلاة، والشفاء، والأساس، والشكر، والدعاء.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
﴿الم﴾: القول الصحيح في الحروف المقطعة أنها أسماء للسور، والأسماء لا تعلل ولا تفسر، وعليه أئمة العلم.
وقيل: لها معنى، ولكن اللّٰه تبارك وتعالى استأثر بعلمه.
وقيل: لها معنى يعرف بالتتبع وإمعان النظر، ثم اختلف القائلون بهذا القول اختلافًا يطول ذكره.
وأحسن ما قيل فيه: إن القرآن مركب من هذه الحروف التي يتخاطبون بها، وقد تحداهم القرآن أن يأتوا بمثله، ولو بسورة.
ومن أسرار هذه الحروف أنها جاءت بحرف واحد، مثل: ﴿ص﴾ و﴿ق﴾، وبحرفين، مثل: ﴿حم﴾، وبثلاثة أحرف، مثل: ﴿الم﴾، وبأربعة، مثل: ﴿المر﴾ و﴿المص﴾، وبخمسة، مثل: ﴿كهيعص﴾.
وكان كلامهم يأتي من حرف إلى خمسة أحرف، لا أكثر من ذلك.
ومثال الحرف الواحد قول الشاعر:
قلنا لها: قفي لنا، قالت: قاف لا تحسبي أنا نسينا الإيجاف
قالت: «قاف»، أي: وقفت.
وذكر ابن جرير وغيره أمثلة أخرى.

chapters.intro_en_source:
The soundest view concerning the disconnected letters is that they are names of the sūrahs. Proper names are not subject to explanation or the search for an underlying cause. This is the position of leading scholars.
It has also been said that they possess a meaning whose knowledge Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has reserved for Himself.
Others have maintained that their meaning can be discovered through careful examination and deep reflection. Those who held this view then differed greatly concerning their interpretation.
The best explanation offered is that the Qur’an is composed of the same letters used by the Arabs in their speech, yet the Qur’an challenged them to produce anything comparable to it, even a single sūrah.
Among the remarkable features of these letters is that they occur in different combinations:
A single letter, such as:
Ṣād and Qāf;
two letters, such as:
Ḥā-Mīm;
three letters, such as:
Alif-Lām-Mīm;
four letters, such as:
Alif-Lām-Mīm-Rā and Alif-Lām-Mīm-Ṣād;
and five letters, such as:
Kāf-Hā-Yā-ʿAyn-Ṣād.
Their own speech likewise employed expressions consisting of between one and five letters, but not more than that.
An example of a single letter being used as a complete expression is the poet’s statement:
We said to her, “Stop for us,” and she replied, “Qāf.”
 Do not imagine that we have forgotten to hasten.
Her reply “Qāf” means:
“I have stopped.”
Ibn Jarīr and others mentioned further examples.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
الكتاب هو القرآن الكريم.
وقوله: ﴿هُدًى لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾، أي: إن التفاصيل الواردة في القرآن من الأوامر والنواهي لا يستفيد منها إلا المتقون، مثل قوله تعالى:
﴿قُلْ هُوَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هُدًى وَشِفَاءٌ﴾ [فصلت: ٤٤].
وأما غير المتقين من الكفار والمشركين، فلهم قوله تعالى:
﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بُرْهَانٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ، وَأَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ نُورًا مُبِينًا﴾ [النساء: ١٧٤].
وقال اللّٰه تعالى:
﴿قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ نُورٌ وَكِتَابٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ [المائدة: ١٥].
وقال تعالى:
﴿الر كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ لِتُخْرِجَ النَّاسَ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ﴾ [إبراهيم: ١].

chapters.intro_en_source:
The Book is the Noble Qur’an.
The words:
“A guidance for the God-fearing”
mean that the detailed commands and prohibitions contained within the Qur’an truly benefit only those who fear Allah.
This resembles the words of Allah, the Exalted:
“Say: It is guidance and healing for those who believe.”
 [Sūrat Fuṣṣilat 41:44]
As for those who are not God-fearing, including the disbelievers and polytheists, the Qur’an remains a universal proof addressed to them, as Allah, the Exalted, said:
“O mankind, there has certainly come to you a conclusive proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light.”
 [Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:174]
Allah, the Exalted, also said:
“There has certainly come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.”
 [Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:15]
And He said:
“Alif-Lām-Rā. This is a Book which We have revealed to you so that you may bring mankind out of darkness into light.”
 [Sūrat Ibrāhīm 14:1]

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قوله: ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾، الغيب يعني كل ما غاب عن الناس، ولا يمكن إدراكه بالحواس، مثل وجود اللّٰه تعالى، والملائكة، واليوم الآخر، وصفة الجنة والنار، وما أعده اللّٰه تعالى من الحياة بعد الموت، إلى غير ذلك مما ذكر في القرآن والسنة الصحيحة.
وقوله: ﴿وَيُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَاةَ﴾، إقامة الصلاة هي أداء الصلاة كاملة، ابتداء من إسباغ الوضوء، وقراءة القرآن، وإتمام الركوع والسجود، والتشهد، والصلاة على النبي ﷺ، مع المحافظة على مواقيتها.

chapters.intro_en_source:
The words:
“Those who believe in the unseen”
refer to everything hidden from human perception and inaccessible to the physical senses.
This includes belief in Allah, the Exalted, the angels, the Last Day, the descriptions of Paradise and Hell, the life which Allah has prepared after death, and all other unseen matters established in the Qur’an and the authentic Sunnah.
The words:
“They establish prayer”
mean performing the prayer completely, beginning with perfecting the ablution, reciting the Qur’an, completing the bowing and prostration properly, reciting the tashahhud, invoking blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, and carefully observing the appointed times of prayer.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قوله: ﴿خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾، وذلك جزاء منه على تماديهم في الباطل وتركهم الحق، لا أنه تعالى ختم على قلوبهم ابتداء.
بل خلقهم كغيرهم على الفطرة، وهداهم النجدين، فلما اختاروا الباطل بمحض إرادتهم ختم اللّٰه على قلوبهم جزاء وفاقًا.
كما قال تعالى:
﴿بَلْ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهَا بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾ [النساء: ١٥٥].
وقال:
﴿كَلَّا بَلْ رَانَ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ مَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ [المطففين: ١٤].

قوله: ﴿خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾، وذلك جزاء منه على تماديهم في الباطل وتركهم الحق، لا أنه تعالى ختم على قلوبهم ابتداء.
بل خلقهم كغيرهم على الفطرة، وهداهم النجدين، فلما اختاروا الباطل بمحض إرادتهم ختم اللّٰه على قلوبهم جزاء وفاقًا.
كما قال تعالى:
﴿بَلْ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهَا بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾ [النساء: ١٥٥].
وقال:
﴿كَلَّا بَلْ رَانَ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ مَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ [المطففين: ١٤].
chapters.intro_en_source:
The words:
“Allah has sealed their hearts”
describe a punishment imposed upon them because they persisted in falsehood and abandoned the truth.
It does not mean that Allah initially sealed their hearts without cause. Rather, He created them upon the natural disposition like all others and showed them the two paths. When they freely chose falsehood, Allah sealed their hearts as a fitting recompense.
Allah, the Exalted, said:
“Rather, Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief.”
 [Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:155]
And He said:
“No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts with rust.”
 [Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn 83:14]

chapters.title_ar: ٤- باب قوله تعالى: ﴿خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعَلَى سَمْعِهِمْ، وَعَلَى أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةٌ، وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾
chapters.title_en: Chapter 4 – The Words of Allah: “Allah Has Sealed Their Hearts and Their Hearing, and over Their Eyes Is a Covering, and They Will Have a Great Punishment”

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قوله: ﴿يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ﴾، أي: يظنون أنهم بإظهار الإيمان وإبطان الكفر يخدعون اللّٰه، فأخبرهم بأنه يعلم ما يظهرون وما يبطنون.
ولذلك رد اللّٰه عليهم بقوله:
﴿وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾.
chapters.intro_ar_display:
قوله: ﴿يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ﴾، أي: يظنون أنهم بإظهار الإيمان وإبطان الكفر يخدعون اللّٰه، فأخبرهم بأنه يعلم ما يظهرون وما يبطنون.
ولذلك رد اللّٰه عليهم بقوله:
﴿وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾.
chapters.intro_en_source:
The words:
“They seek to deceive Allah”
mean that they imagine that by displaying faith outwardly while concealing disbelief inwardly, they can deceive Allah.
He informed them that He knows both what they reveal and what they conceal.
Allah therefore answered them with His words:
“They deceive none except themselves, though they do not realize it.”

chapters.title_ar: ٥- باب قوله تعالى: ﴿يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا، وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾
chapters.title_en: Chapter 5 – The Words of Allah: “They Seek to Deceive Allah and Those Who Believe, but They Deceive None except Themselves, Though They Do Not Realize It”

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قوله: ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾، المرض هو الشك، وقيل: هو النفاق، يعني مرضًا في الدين، لا في الأجساد.
وقوله: ﴿فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا﴾، أي: كلما ازدادوا في شكهم ونفاقهم ازدادوا في مرضهم.
chapters.intro_ar_display:
قوله: ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾، المرض هو الشك، وقيل: هو النفاق، يعني مرضًا في الدين، لا في الأجساد.
وقوله: ﴿فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا﴾، أي: كلما ازدادوا في شكهم ونفاقهم ازدادوا في مرضهم.
chapters.intro_en_source:
The words:
“In their hearts is a disease”
refer to doubt.
It has also been said that the disease is hypocrisy. It is a disease affecting their religion, not their physical bodies.
The words:
“So Allah increased their disease”
mean that whenever they increased in doubt and hypocrisy, they increased in spiritual illness.

chapters.title_ar: ٦- باب قوله تعالى: ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا، وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ﴾
chapters.title_en: Chapter 6 – The Words of Allah: “In Their Hearts Is a Disease, so Allah Increased Their Disease, and They Will Have a Painful Punishment because They Used to Lie”

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قوله: ﴿لَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾، الفساد في الأرض هو الكفر والعمل بالمعصية. قال به جماعة من الصحابة، منهم ابن مسعود وابن عباس؛ لأن عمارة الأرض لا تكون إلا بالطاعة.
وقوله: ﴿قَالُوا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ﴾، أي: نحن على الهدى والرشاد.
فقال اللّٰه تعالى:
﴿أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ وَلَكِنْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾.
أي: إنهم على الكفر والضلال والنفاق، فهم المفسدون حقًا، وإن كانوا يدعون أنهم يحسنون صنعًا.
وقوله: ﴿وَلَكِنْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾، من جهلهم وبغضهم للّٰه ورسوله ولكتابه.

chapters.intro_en_source:
The words:
“Do not spread corruption upon the earth”
refer to disbelief and acts of disobedience.
A group of the Companions, including Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, held this interpretation, because the earth can only be properly cultivated through obedience to Allah.
Their words:
“We are only reformers”
mean:
“We are upon guidance and sound judgment.”
Allah, the Exalted, replied:
“Indeed, they are the corruptors, but they do not realize it.”
They are upon disbelief, misguidance, and hypocrisy. They are therefore the true corrupters, even though they claim that they are doing good.
The words:
“But they do not realize it”
refer to their ignorance and their hatred for Allah, His Messenger, and His Book.

chapters.title_ar: ٧- باب قوله تعالى: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ قَالُوا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ ۝ أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ وَلَكِنْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾
chapters.title_en: Chapter 7 – The Words of Allah: “When It Is Said to Them, ‘Do Not Spread Corruption upon the Earth,’ They Say, ‘We Are Only Reformers.’ Indeed, They Are the Corruptors, but They Do Not Realize It”

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قوله تعالى: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ﴾، أي: للمنافقين الذين أظهروا الإسلام وأبطنوا الكفر؛ فإنهم كانوا يقولون فيما بينهم: هل نحن نؤمن كما آمن هؤلاء السفهاء، يعنون أصحاب محمد ﷺ؟
فرد اللّٰه عليهم بقوله:
﴿أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ السُّفَهَاءُ﴾.
والسفيه هو الذي يجهل مصالح نفسه فيضرها، وهذه الصفة منطبقة عليهم.

chapters.intro_en_source:
The words:
“When it is said to them”
refer to the hypocrites who outwardly displayed Islam while inwardly concealing disbelief.
They would say among themselves:
“Should we believe as these foolish people have believed?”
They meant the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ.
Allah answered them with His words:
“Indeed, it is they who are the foolish.”
A foolish person is one who remains ignorant of what benefits him and consequently harms himself.
This description applies perfectly to them.

chapters.title_ar: ٨- باب قوله تعالى: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُوا كَمَا آمَنَ النَّاسُ قَالُوا أَنُؤْمِنُ كَمَا آمَنَ السُّفَهَاءُ أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ السُّفَهَاءُ وَلَكِنْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾
chapters.title_en: Chapter 8 – The Words of Allah: “When It Is Said to Them, ‘Believe as the People Have Believed,’ They Say, ‘Should We Believe as the Foolish Have Believed?’ Indeed, It Is They Who Are the Foolish, but They Do Not Know”

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قوله: ﴿إِلَى شَيَاطِينِهِمْ﴾، أي: إلى رؤسائهم وكبرائهم، وهم أحبار اليهود والكفار والمشركون.
والمراد بالشياطين هنا شياطين الإنس؛ لأن الشياطين يكونون من الإنس كما يكونون من الجن، لقوله تعالى:
﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا شَيَاطِينَ الْإِنْسِ وَالْجِنِّ، يُوحِي بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَى بَعْضٍ زُخْرُفَ الْقَوْلِ غُرُورًا﴾ [الأنعام: ١١٢].
وشياطين الإنس هم من يظهر أمام الناس بأنه مخلص لهم في عمله وقوله، وهو من أفسق الناس وأفسدهم.
وقوله: ﴿إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾، أي: نسخر بأصحاب محمد ﷺ، فنقول لهم: نحن مؤمنون كما أنتم مؤمنون.
ورد اللّٰه عليهم بقوله: ﴿اللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ﴾، أي: على وجه المقابلة، لا على وجه الإطلاق؛ لأنه في حال المقابلة يدل على القوة والكمال والعدل، بخلاف حال الابتداء فإنه يدل على الذم.
ولذا روي عن ابن عباس: «يسخر بهم للنقمة منهم».
وكذلك قوله تعالى:
﴿وَمَكَرُوا وَمَكَرَ اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ﴾ [آل عمران: ٥٤].
وكذلك قوله تعالى:
﴿يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وَهُوَ خَادِعُهُمْ﴾ [النساء: ١٤٢].
وأشباه ذلك كثير في كتاب اللّٰه.
وقوله: ﴿وَيَمُدُّهُمْ﴾، أي: يملي لهم ويمهلهم.

chapters.intro_en_source:
The words:
“To their devils”
refer to their leaders and prominent figures, including the rabbis of the Jews, the disbelievers, and the polytheists.
The devils intended here are human devils, because devils may be from mankind just as they may be from the jinn.
Allah, the Exalted, said:
“In this way We made for every prophet enemies—devils from mankind and jinn—inspiring one another with decorative speech as deception.”
 [Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:112]
Human devils are those who appear before people as though they are sincere in their actions and words, while in reality they are among the most wicked and corrupt of people.
Their words:
“We were only mocking”
mean:
“We are mocking the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ by telling them that we believe just as they believe.”
Allah answered them with His words:
“Allah repays their mockery.”
This is stated as a fitting response to their conduct, not as an unrestricted description.
When mentioned in the context of just retribution, it indicates power, perfection, and justice. If initiated without such a context, mockery would be blameworthy.
It is therefore reported from Ibn ʿAbbās:
“He subjects them to mockery as a punishment and vengeance against them.”
This resembles the words of Allah, the Exalted:
“They plotted, and Allah planned, and Allah is the best of planners.”
 [Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:54]
And His words:
“They seek to deceive Allah, but He repays their deception.”
 [Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:142]
Many similar examples occur in the Book of Allah.
The words:
“And He leaves them”
mean that Allah grants them respite and allows them time.

chapters.title_ar: ٩- باب قوله تعالى: ﴿وَإِذَا لَقُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قَالُوا آمَنَّا، وَإِذَا خَلَوْا إِلَى شَيَاطِينِهِمْ قَالُوا إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِئُونَ ۝ اللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ وَيَمُدُّهُمْ فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾
chapters.title_en: Chapter 9 – The Words of Allah: “When They Meet Those Who Believe, They Say, ‘We Believe,’ but When They Withdraw to Their Devils, They Say, ‘We Are with You; We Were Only Mocking.’ Allah Repays Their Mockery and Leaves Them Wandering Blindly in Their Transgression”

chapters.intro_ar_source:
ضرب اللّٰه مثل المنافقين بأنهم لو كانوا مؤمنين حقًا، لكان مثلهم مثل الذي استوقد نارًا فأضاءت ما حوله.
ولكنهم لم يؤمنوا، وإنما كفروا ونافقوا، فصاروا كالذي ذهب اللّٰه بنوره، فصار كل شيء حوله ظلمات.
وفي هذه الظلمات هم مثل الصم الذي لا يسمع الخير، والبكم الذي لا ينطق بالحق، والأعمى الذي لا يبصر الحق. فمهما أفهمتهم فهم لا يرجعون إليه.

chapters.intro_en_source:
Allah presents the example of the hypocrites.
Had they truly believed, they would have resembled a person who kindled a fire that illuminated everything around him.
But they did not truly believe. Instead, they disbelieved and acted hypocritically.
They therefore became like one whose light Allah removed, leaving everything around him in darkness.
Within this darkness, they are like the deaf person who cannot hear goodness, the mute person who does not speak the truth, and the blind person who cannot see the truth.
No matter how clearly the truth is explained to them, they do not return to it.

chapters.title_en: Chapter 10 – The Words of Allah: “Their Example Is That of One Who Kindled a Fire, but When It Illuminated What Was around Him, Allah Took Away Their Light and Left Them in Darkness, Unable to See—Deaf, Mute, and Blind, so They Will Not Return”

chapters.intro_ar_source: الصيب هو المطر، كما جاء في الصحيح.
chapters.intro_ar_display: الصيب هو المطر، كما جاء في الصحيح.
chapters.intro_en_source: The word al-ṣayyib means rain, as established in the authentic narration.

chapters.title_ar: ١١- باب قوله تعالى: ﴿أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ، يَجْعَلُونَ أَصَابِعَهُمْ فِي آذَانِهِمْ مِنَ الصَّوَاعِقِ حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ، وَاللَّهُ مُحِيطٌ بِالْكَافِرِينَ ۝ يَكَادُ الْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ، كُلَّمَا أَضَاءَ لَهُمْ مَشَوْا فِيهِ، وَإِذَا أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوا، وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَارِهِمْ، إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾
chapters.title_en: Chapter 11 – The Words of Allah: “Or Like a Rainstorm from the Sky within Which Are Darkness, Thunder, and Lightning…”

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قوله: ﴿اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ﴾، أي: وحدوا ربكم؛ لأنه هو الخالق، فهو المستحق للعبادة وحده.
وقوله: ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً﴾، السماء هي كل ما علا فوقك، والمراد بها هنا السحاب.
وقوله: ﴿أَنْدَادًا﴾، جمع ند، وهو النظير والشبيه.

chapters.intro_en_source:
The words:
“Worship your Lord”
mean:
“Single out your Lord alone for worship.”
Because He alone is the Creator, He alone deserves to be worshipped.
The words:
“He sent down water from the sky”
use the word sky for whatever is above a person.
What is intended here is the clouds.
The word:
“Rivals”
is the plural of nidd, meaning an equal, counterpart, or likeness.

chapters.title_ar: ١٢- باب قوله تعالى: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ ۝ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ فِرَاشًا وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً، وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً، فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ رِزْقًا لَكُمْ، فَلَا تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَنْدَادًا وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾
chapters.title_en: Chapter 12 – The Words of Allah: “O Mankind, Worship Your Lord Who Created You and Those before You, so That You May Become God-Fearing…”

chapters.intro_ar_source:
تحدى اللّٰه في مكة والمدينة، في غير موضع من القرآن، أن يأتوا بمثل القرآن، فقال:
﴿قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِكِتَابٍ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ هُوَ أَهْدَىٰ مِنْهُمَا أَتَّبِعْهُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ [القصص: ٤٩].
وقال:
﴿قُلْ لَئِنِ اجْتَمَعَتِ الْإِنْسُ وَالْجِنُّ عَلَىٰ أَنْ يَأْتُوا بِمِثْلِ هَذَا الْقُرْآنِ لَا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِ، وَلَوْ كَانَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ ظَهِيرًا﴾ [الإسراء: ٨٨].
وقال:
﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَاهُ، قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِعَشْرِ سُوَرٍ مِثْلِهِ مُفْتَرَيَاتٍ، وَادْعُوا مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ [هود: ١٣].
وقال:
﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَاهُ، قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِسُورَةٍ مِثْلِهِ، وَادْعُوا مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ [يونس: ٣٨].
وكل هذه الآيات مكية.
وتحداهم في المدينة بقوله:
﴿وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوا بِسُورَةٍ مِنْ مِثْلِهِ﴾.
ويبقى هذا التحدي قائمًا إلى يومنا هذا، وسيستمر إلى يوم القيامة. فليس لمخلوق أن يأتي بمثل كلام الخالق؛ لأن النبي ﷺ خص بهذا القرآن، وهو من أكبر الآيات البينات لنبوة محمد ﷺ، كما جاء في الصحيح:

chapters.intro_en_source:
Allah challenged them in both Makkah and Madinah, in several places of the Qur’an, to produce anything comparable to the Qur’an.
He said:
“Say: Then bring a book from Allah that provides better guidance than these two, and I will follow it, if you are truthful.”
 [Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ 28:49]
And He said:
“Say: If mankind and the jinn were to gather together to produce the like of this Qur’an, they could not produce its like, even if they supported one another.”
 [Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:88]
And He said:
“Or do they say, ‘He has fabricated it’? Say: Then produce ten fabricated sūrahs like it and call upon whomever you are able besides Allah, if you are truthful.”
 [Sūrat Hūd 11:13]
And He said:
“Or do they say, ‘He has fabricated it’? Say: Then produce a sūrah like it and call upon whomever you are able besides Allah, if you are truthful.”
 [Sūrat Yūnus 10:38]
All of these verses are Makkan.
In Madinah, He challenged them with His words:
“If you are in doubt concerning what We have revealed to Our servant, then produce a sūrah like it.”
This challenge remains in force until the present day and will continue until the Day of Resurrection.
No created being can produce anything comparable to the speech of the Creator. The Prophet ﷺ was uniquely granted this Qur’an, and it is among the greatest clear signs proving the prophethood of Muḥammad ﷺ, as stated in the authentic hadith.

chapters.title_en: Chapter 13 – The Words of Allah: “If You Are in Doubt concerning What We Have Revealed to Our Servant, Then Produce a Sūrah Like It…”

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قوله: ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾، أي: في الدنيا، كما قال به ابن مسعود وابن عباس وغيرهما من السلف. وقول من قال: إنه في الجنة، قول مرجوح.
وقوله: ﴿وَأُتُوا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا﴾، أي: متشابهًا في الاسم مع اختلاف الطعم، كما جاء عن ابن عباس، قال: ليس في الجنة شيء يشبه ما في الدنيا.
رواه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره (١٠/٦٦)، وابن جرير في تفسيره.
وقيل: التشابه في ثمار الجنة في اللون، وليس في الاسم والطعم. وقيل غير ذلك، وكله صحيح لا يعارض بعضه بعضًا؛ فإن الآية تشمل كل هذه الوجوه.
وقوله: ﴿مُطَهَّرَةٌ﴾، أي: مطهرة من الحيض. وأما بقية الأذى من البول والبراز وغيرها، فهن مثل الرجال، كما جاء في الصحيح.

chapters.intro_en_source:
The words:
“Before this”
mean in the worldly life, according to Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and other early scholars.
The view that it means they had previously received it within Paradise is the weaker opinion.
The words:
“They will be given fruit resembling it”
mean that it resembles worldly fruit in name while differing in taste.
Ibn ʿAbbās said:
“Nothing in Paradise truly resembles what is in the world.”
Narrated by Ibn Abī Ḥātim in his Tafsīr (10/66) and by Ibn Jarīr in his Tafsīr.
It has also been said that the fruits of Paradise resemble one another in color while differing in name and taste.
Other interpretations have also been offered. All of them are valid and do not contradict one another, because the verse encompasses all these meanings.
The word:
“Purified”
means purified from menstruation.
As for other bodily impurities, such as urination and defecation, the women of Paradise, like its men, will be entirely free from them, as stated in the authentic hadith.

chapters.title_ar: ١٤- باب قوله تعالى: ﴿وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ، كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوا مِنْهَا مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ رِزْقًا قَالُوا هَذَا الَّذِي رُزِقْنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ، وَأُتُوا بِهِ مُتَشَابِهًا، وَلَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ، وَهُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾
chapters.title_en: Chapter 14 – The Words of Allah: “Give Glad Tidings to Those Who Believe and Perform Righteous Deeds That They Will Have Gardens beneath Which Rivers Flow…”

chapters.intro_ar_source:
اعترض الكفار على ضرب اللّٰه المثل في قوله:
﴿مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي اسْتَوْقَدَ نَارًا﴾،
وفي قوله:
﴿أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾.
فرد اللّٰه عليهم بقوله:
﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَسْتَحْيِي أَنْ يَضْرِبَ مَثَلًا مَا بَعُوضَةً فَمَا فَوْقَهَا﴾؛
لأن ضرب الأمثال من أفصح الكلام.
ولذلك قال اللّٰه تعالى في موضع آخر:
﴿وَتِلْكَ الْأَمْثَالُ نَضْرِبُهَا لِلنَّاسِ، وَمَا يَعْقِلُهَا إِلَّا الْعَالِمُونَ﴾ [العنكبوت: ٤٣].
وقوله تعالى: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَسْتَحْيِي أَنْ يَضْرِبَ مَثَلًا مَا بَعُوضَةً فَمَا فَوْقَهَا﴾، يعني: يصح ضرب المثل بالصغير كما يصح بالكبير؛ لأن المقصود من ضرب المثل تقريب المعاني وإفهامها، بغض النظر عن كون المذكور حقيرًا أو عظيمًا.
ولذلك إذا ضرب اللّٰه مثلًا ازداد المؤمن إيمانًا، والكافر كفرًا، والمنافق نفاقًا.
وقوله: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَنْقُضُونَ عَهْدَ اللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مِيثَاقِهِ﴾، أي: هم المنافقون الذين أعلنوا إسلامهم، فلما ضرب اللّٰه مثلًا ارتابوا فيه، فنقضوا عهد اللّٰه، وهو الإيمان باللّٰه، وتركوا أوامره، وأفسدوا في الأرض، فهم الخاسرون في الدنيا والآخرة.

chapters.intro_en_source:
The disbelievers objected to the examples Allah presented in His words:
“Their example is that of one who kindled a fire,”
and:
“Or like a rainstorm from the sky.”
Allah answered them with His words:
“Allah is not ashamed to present an example, even of a mosquito or something beyond it.”
Presenting examples is among the most eloquent forms of speech.
Allah, the Exalted, therefore said elsewhere:
“These are the examples We present to mankind, but none understands them except those who possess knowledge.”
 [Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt 29:43]
The words of Allah:
“Allah is not ashamed to present an example, even of a mosquito or something beyond it”
mean that an example may appropriately be presented using something small just as it may be presented using something great.
The purpose of an example is to make meanings accessible and understandable, regardless of whether the object mentioned is insignificant or magnificent.
Thus, when Allah presents an example, the believer increases in faith, the disbeliever increases in disbelief, and the hypocrite increases in hypocrisy.
The words:
“Those who break Allah’s covenant after it has been confirmed”
refer to the hypocrites who outwardly announced their acceptance of Islam.
When Allah presented an example, they doubted it and broke their covenant with Allah, which was faith in Him. They abandoned His commands and spread corruption upon the earth. They are therefore the losers in this world and the Hereafter.

chapters.title_en: Chapter 15 – The Words of Allah: “Allah Is Not Ashamed to Present an Example, Even of a Mosquito or Something beyond It…”

chapters.intro_ar_source:
ثم أقام اللّٰه الحجة عليهم بأنهم كانوا في أصلاب آبائهم أمواتًا، ثم أخرجهم أحياء، ثم يميتهم موت الدنيا، ثم يحييهم حياة الآخرة.
فيعترفون يوم القيامة بحياتين وميتتين، كما في سورة غافر:
﴿قَالُوا رَبَّنَا أَمَتَّنَا اثْنَتَيْنِ وَأَحْيَيْتَنَا اثْنَتَيْنِ، فَاعْتَرَفْنَا بِذُنُوبِنَا، فَهَلْ إِلَىٰ خُرُوجٍ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ﴾ [غافر: ١١].

chapters.intro_en_source:
Allah then established the proof against them.
They were lifeless within the loins of their fathers. He then brought them forth alive, will cause them to die the death of this world, and will afterward bring them to life for the Hereafter.
On the Day of Resurrection, they will acknowledge two deaths and two lives, as stated in Sūrat Ghāfir:
“They will say: Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and gave us life twice. We now confess our sins, so is there any way out?”
 [Sūrat Ghāfir 40:11]

chapters.title_ar: ١٦- باب قوله تعالى: ﴿كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَكُنْتُمْ أَمْوَاتًا فَأَحْيَاكُمْ، ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ، ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾
chapters.title_en: Chapter 16 – The Words of Allah: “How Can You Disbelieve in Allah when You Were Lifeless and He Gave You Life?”

chapters.intro_ar_source:
هذا دليل آخر على عظمة اللّٰه وقدرته.
وقوله: ﴿لَكُمْ﴾، دليل على الانتفاع بما خلق اللّٰه في السماوات والأرض. واللّٰه تعالى لا يمتن علينا بشيء إلا أن يكون فيه نفع لنا.
وفيه إشارة إلى الابتعاد عن كل ما فيه ضرر للإنسان، سواء كان من الخبائث التي ورد تحريمها في النصوص، أو من الفساد الذي يدمر حرث الأرض.
وقوله: ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ﴾، أي: قصد وأقبل؛ لأن الاستواء إذا تعدى بـ«إلى» فمعناه قصد.
وإذا تعدى بـ«على» فمعناه ارتفع، كما في قوله تعالى:
﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾ [الأعراف: ٥٤].
وإذا ذكر من غير حرف يكون معناه الكمال والتمام، كقوله تعالى عن موسى:
﴿وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَاسْتَوَىٰ﴾ [القصص: ١٤].
وهنا ذكر بحرف «إلى»، فمعناه أن اللّٰه بعد أن خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعًا لتنتفعوا بها، قصد إلى خلق السماوات السبع، مع شموسها، وأقمارها، ونجومها، وفضائها، ومن فيهن، لتنتفعوا بها.
وقوله: ﴿وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾، أي: إنه يعلم احتياجكم؛ ولذلك خلق لكم ما في الأرض وما في السماوات.
وهنا لا يقصد اللّٰه سبحانه وتعالى أن يبين مراحل خلق الأرض والسماوات، بل المقصود امتنانه على عباده بأن هذه المخلوقات خلقها اللّٰه تعالى لينتفع بها الإنسان.
